title: Digital Biomarkers in Rare Neurodegenerative Diseases: Smartwatch-based Longitudinal Monitoring and AI-based Gait Analysis
summary:
Rare diseases such as Wilson disease and Huntington disease can cause progressive problems with movement, thinking, and everyday activities. Disease progression is currently assessed mainly during individual medical appointments. As a result, changes occurring between appointments may remain undetected.

This study investigates whether a smartwatch and computer-assisted gait analysis can enable more continuous and objective monitoring. Participants wear a smartwatch for twelve months. It records, among other things, movement, step count, heart rate, and sleep. At the beginning and after twelve months, participants also undergo clinical examinations, questionnaires, blood tests, and a short gait analysis. Further follow-up assessments take place after three and six months; some of these assessments can be performed by video consultation.

The smartwatch and gait-analysis results are compared with medical examinations, cognitive tests, questionnaires, and blood-test results. The study also assesses how well participants can use the smartwatch in everyday life. The study does not change medical treatment. No new medication is administered and no genetic testing is performed.

interventions.name: Prospective longitudinal observation with diagnostic elements of patients with Wilson disease, Huntington disease, and individuals at risk of Huntington disease over a period of twelve months. criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Adults aged 18 years or older who are capable of providing informed consent and have a confirmed diagnosis of a rare neurodegenerative disease. Eligible participants include patients with Wilson disease confirmed by an ATP7B mutation or diagnostically conclusive laboratory findings, as well as patients with Huntington disease and a confirmed CAG expansion. Huntington disease at-risk individuals with a known 50% genetic risk may also be included. No genetic testing will be performed as part of the study. Participants must have a smartphone compatible with the Withings app (at least iOS 16 or Android 12). The ability to stand or walk is not required. Women of childbearing potential without contraception, pregnant women, and breastfeeding women may be included.
Exclusion criteria:
Severe cognitive impairment with a MoCA score below 15 points, insufficient smartphone compatibility with the Withings app, inability to understand or operate the smartwatch, insufficient language comprehension of the smartwatch user interface, acute psychiatric decompensation, or a life expectancy of less than 12 months. Inability to stand or walk is not an exclusion criterion; in such cases, AI-based gait analysis and the TUG and POMA tests will not be performed.
